title: Degreewise ordinary evaluation and coefficient augmentation
statement: For a scheme Y and module-sheaf cochain complexes P,N, let I be the fixed K-injective resolution of N. Define E_n:Tot(Hom(P,N) tensor P)^n to N^n by coproduct descent: on the (p,q) summand, p+q=n, it is symmetry followed by inverse tensor-Hom adjunction applied to the fixed Hom projection Hom(P,N)^p to Hom(P^q,N^n). For every morphism g:N to I and every integer n, the degree-n component of schemeTensorHomUncurry of Hom(P,g) equals E_n followed by g^n. This is an equality of explicitly defined graded maps; it asserts neither existence nor differential compatibility of an evaluation chain map.

source.place: Tags 08DJ (lemma-internal-hom), 08DM and 08DQ; ordinary evaluation localization proof step 2

proof.text: Use coproduct extensionality and the summand formula for schemeTensorHomUncurry. For p+q=n, rewrite its summand as symmetry followed by inverse tensor-Hom adjunction of Hom(P,g)^p followed by the projection to Hom(P^q,I^n), where I is the fixed resolution of N.

The coefficient naturality formula for the fixed Hom projections, with identity on P, replaces the projected Hom(P,g) map by the projection to Hom(P^q,N^n) followed by homObjMap(id,g^n). The small homComplex_projections_exists API selects the same projection witness as homComplex_exists, so these component descriptions agree.

Naturality of the tensor-Hom equivalence in the coefficient moves g^n outside inverse adjunction. Compose with symmetry and use associativity and the mapBifunctorDesc summand equation. This gives equality on every summand and hence in total degree n. No differential equation or monicity is needed.

theorem schemeOrdinaryEvaluationGraded_augmentation (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (P N : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (g : N ⟶ (schemeHomKInjectiveResolution Y).obj N) (n : ℤ) :
    (schemeTensorHomUncurry Y (homComplex (R := Y.sheaf) P N) P N
      (((homComplexFunctor (R := Y.sheaf)).obj (op P)).map g)).f n =
        schemeOrdinaryEvaluationGraded Y P N n ≫ g.f n
